## Dropped

- `README.md`: it names the private repository.
- `tools/action.yml`: a composite action for the private fix pipeline, not used by review.
- `tools/review/angles/`: the default angle prompts; the Drupal prompts `bugs.md` and `security.md` replace them, so a missing Drupal prompt fails instead of falling back.
- The steps "Keep the review trace" and "Archive the review trace": traces would be public here.
- The eval's "Keep the scores" artifact step: the artifact would be public here.
- `.github/workflows/test.yml`: its test steps are ported into this repository's own workflow.

## Renamed

- The helper folder is `tools/agent/` (D21).
- Its variables are `AGENT_ARGS_*`, `AGENT_MODEL_*`, `AGENT_TURNS_*` and `AGENT_BLOCK_*` (D21).

The reviewer tools CI job refreshes its package lists and installs ripgrep for it.
- `tools/review/check-trace-tools.sh`, `tools/review/check-trace-tools.test.sh`, `tools/review/check-trace-tools-ripgrep.test.sh`, `tools/review/search-rules.md`: the whole-glob entry. A Grep `glob` is judged whole, as ripgrep matches an override glob, instead of segment by segment. Each comma part and brace expansion is refused when, with no `/` (a trailing `/` aside), it can match the name `.git`, or, with a `/`, it can match `.git`'s path (`.git`, and from a root above the workspace also `repo/.git`) or names `.git` on the way to a path inside it (`.git/config`, `**/.git/**`); matching ignores letter case; `..` and a leading `!` are still refused. Brace lists of folders such as `{scripts/*,web/modules/custom/**}` and `*/x.php` now pass, and `*`, `**`, `**/*`, `.g*`, `*/` and `**/.git` do not. The canary adds folder-list shapes and counts a glob ripgrep cannot parse (nested brace groups) as unparsed rather than an error. The six audit prompts state the same rule.
- `tools/review/check-trace-tools.sh`, `tools/review/check-trace-tools.test.sh`, `tools/review/check-trace-tools-ripgrep.test.sh`, `tools/review/search-rules.md`: where the whole-glob rule applies, a Grep `path` whose raw value holds a `..` segment is refused (label `Grep path holds a .. segment`), and so is one with a symlink on disk at check time in a component below the allowed root that holds it (label `Grep path passes through a symlink`; the root and its ancestors are not judged, so a workspace behind a symlink still works), since ripgrep matches a glob against the path as written and follows a symlinked folder: `web/..` with `web/**`, `<workspace>/..` with `*/repo/**` from an added root, and a folder linked to the checkout with `web/**` returned `.git` files with ripgrep 13.0.0. With `--grep-any-glob-in-subfolders`, a path through a symlink no longer counts as a subfolder and falls to the same rule; before this, a folder linked to the checkout took any glob and `*` returned `.git` files, a hole the check already had before the whole-glob entry. The canary searches every accepted call both as Claude Code 2.1.309 spawns ripgrep for a folder on Linux (it opens the path and runs ripgrep in `/proc/self/fd/<fd>` with `.` as the target) and by the raw path, for no path, the checkout, a subfolder, `src/..`, `<checkout>/..` and the parent as an added root, and folders linked to the checkout and to its parent, with and without the audit options; it requires the three leaking calls to be refused, refused globs to leak in both spawn modes, and every glob ripgrep cannot parse to hold a nested brace group. When the workspace's real path differs from its spelling, a Grep glob is also judged against `.git`'s absolute paths, spelled and real, since ripgrep run in the workspace with the spelled path as its target matches the absolute path (`*/*/**` returned `.git` files there). The canary runs in a plain layout and with the checkout's parent behind a symlink. The six audit prompts state the symlink rule.

Before this, with the workspace spelled through a link and an added root given by its real path, a Grep at that root with `*` or `repo/**` passed and ripgrep returned `repo/.git` files, and a root, head link or input link pointing into or above the checkout was trusted the same way. A search root spelled through a link adds its absolute spelling of `.git` as a target. Where the glob rule applies, the glob is judged first, then whether the path lies in a root, then the `..`, normal-form and symlink checks. A Grep path that is not in normal form (`//`, `/./`, a trailing `/.`) is refused with the label `Grep path is not in normal form`; a leading `./` and a trailing `/` still pass. The canary adds the parent as a root by its real path and through a link, head and input links to the checkout and its parent, and the non-normal spellings, and checks each regression call's label. The search rules and the six audit prompts say to give a path inside the checkout that does not pass through a symbolic link.

A `!` anywhere but the start of a part (`{!a,b}`, `a/!b`) is a literal character to ripgrep (measured with rg 13.0.0 and Claude Code's rg 14.1.1) and is refused. Subfolder mode, which already took `!` anywhere, is unchanged. A glob kept whole because it holds a brace group, that starts with `!` and has a comma outside its braces (`!web/**,{a/**,z.php}`), is refused in every mode, since ripgrep reads that comma literally and the exclusion does nothing. The canary adds negated parts alone, beside every folder shape and in pairs, and inner-`!` controls. A Grep glob that holds a brace group and also a comma outside it is refused whatever its first character. `tools/review/grep_glob_parts.py` (new) holds Claude Code's split of a Grep glob for the check; the canary keeps its own model and fails if the two disagree on a fixed corpus. The six audit prompts state the same rule.

In such a glob a `!` after the first character passes the character allowlist as the literal character ripgrep reads it as, and the glob is never treated as an exclusion unless it starts with `!`, so `{!re,x},po/**` from above a checkout named `!re,po` is refused (both measured with rg 13.0.0 and Claude Code 2.1.316's rg 14.1.1). It passes when every brace expansion is an absolute path in normal form (no empty, `.` or `..` segment, no trailing `/`); that directory, the same directory of each expansion and each expansion whole lie inside the roots and outside `.git` in both views; none of those directories passes through a symlink below its root; and, where `.git` lies below that directory, no expansion's glob can match `.git` or a path below it, judged by `can_reach_git` in a new listed mode (a glob with no `/` reaches it whenever `.git` is below, and a glob with a `/` when it can match any path below `.git`, so `*/config`, `**`, `.g*/config` and `*/.git/config` from above are refused). A pattern not in normal form, or through a symlink to a folder inside the roots, keeps the label `Glob pattern is absolute`; one outside the roots, a symlink leading outside them included (its real path is judged first), gets `path outside the allowed roots`, and one under `.git` or able to reach it `path under .git`. It is judged against `.git` as ripgrep reads it: each brace expansion is a positive glob with its `!` in place, so from above a checkout named `!re` the globs `{x/**,!re/**}`, `{x,!r*}/**` and `{!re/**}` are refused, and a glob whose first character is `!` stays an exclusion that only removes files (`!{x,!re}/**` passes). A `!` after the first character of a part Claude Code splits off with no brace group (`a/!b`, `x,a/!b`) is still refused as a character outside the allowlist; a `!` after a `/` outside the braces of a kept-whole glob (`{a,b}/!c`, `x,{a,b}/!c`) is warned about like one inside them. The search rules and the six audit prompts say such a `!` excludes nothing and to write each exclusion as its own comma part starting with `!`.
- `tools/review/check-trace-tools.sh`, `tools/review/check-trace-tools.test.sh`, `tools/review/check-trace-tools-ripgrep.test.sh`, `tools/review/search-rules.md`: a `**` at the edge of a brace alternative. ripgrep's globset (the same parser in rg 13.0.0's 0.4.8 and Claude Code's rg 14.1.1's 0.4.15) compiles a brace group as a regex alternation of its raw tokens: an alternative starting with `**/` reads it as `(?:/?|.*/)` and one ending with `/**` as `/.*`, whatever surrounds the group, while the brace expansion splices the alternative onto its neighbours. So `*{**/.git,**/*}`, `*{**/git,**/config}` and `*{**/it,**/config}` (expanded `***/.git`, `***/git`, read as one segment) were accepted with no path and returned `.git/config` with both ripgreps, `r*{**/o/.git,**/o/.git/*}` from the parent as an added root returned `repo/.git/config`, and in a workspace behind a symlinked parent the raw path leaked for `{/,z}<parent>/r*{**/o/.git,**/o/.git/*}` and for `{/<first>/**,z}<rest of parent>/repo/{.git,.git/*}`. A brace alternative that starts with `**/` is now refused unless its group starts the glob or follows a `/`, with the label `glob holds ** at the edge of a brace alternative that is not a whole path segment`, for Grep globs (where the `.git` rule applies, exclusion parts aside) and absolute Glob patterns; every group counts, nested ones too. A `**` after a `/` and before anything but a `/` in an expansion is judged as `**/*`, which is exactly `/.*`, so an alternative ending with `/**` needs no refusal and the audit's `{modules/custom/**,themes/custom/**},!**/node_modules/**` still passes with its warning. A `**` at the start of an alternative not followed by `/` is two `*` within a segment to globset and passes when it cannot reach `.git` (`.{**.git}/*`). Measured with both ripgreps over 7356 generated shapes: for each of the 4120 the rule accepts, ripgrep's listing of the raw glob lies within its listing of the rewritten expansions (16 do not without the `/**` rewrite). Accepted on main and now refused: `a{**/.git,y}`, `{x,y}{**/.git}`, `*{**/x}/*`, `src{**/*.php,x}`, `x{**/repo/.git}` and `<checkout>/src/x{**/*.php}`, all synthetic. `check-agent-run.sh` does not use this matcher (its isolation targets are the literal folders before the first wildcard segment), so it is unchanged. The canary adds groups whose alternatives start or end with `**` after eight prefixes, pairs of such alternatives after `*` and letters, the linked-parent shapes above and absolute patterns of these shapes, and fails if any of those regression globs is accepted or stops returning the token. The search rules and the six audit prompts say where a brace alternative may start with `**/`.
